correctness.rationale: Exact first-order RKC Chebyshev stage recurrence yields the affine shared-sample update. Strict interior contraction follows from positive damping and even Chebyshev parity. The random series proves stationarity and variance; two-map hull coverage establishes the support criterion; the s simple zeros and s-1 internal extrema establish the component count; the negative extrema attain the exact sharp variance bound and solve the unique damping threshold. Independent rational stage recurrences, exhaustive sign-history moments and extrema were replayed from verify.py, 25,394 checks. The analytic steps, not numerical extrapolation, prove the infinite claims.

value.rationale: Constant-step stochastic stabilized descent is motivated by the primary paper, which introduces positive damping to avoid Chebyshev neutral points. The theorem identifies exactly how much damping controls the worst stationary error uniformly across the entire stability interval and discovers that the same sharp parameter merges all separated noninterval-support windows. The all-even-stage classification can benchmark damping selection and distinguishes support geometry from mean-square stability; it is not an arbitrary finite table or a generalization by parameter renaming.
